what_its_for: Certolizumab pegol is used to reduce swelling, pain, and stiffness caused by certain conditions where your immune system attacks your own body. These conditions include rheumatoid arthritis (RA), psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis (a type of spine inflammation), non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, and Crohn's disease. It works by blocking a protein in your body called TNF-alpha that causes inflammation.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your stomach area or thigh. You or a caregiver can give the injection at home after proper training by your healthcare provider. The medicine comes as a prefilled syringe or autoinjector pen. Always rotate your injection sites and avoid injecting into skin that is bruised, red, hard, or tender. Let the syringe or pen warm up to room temperature for about 30 minutes before injecting — do not microwave or heat it. Follow your doctor's exact instructions on how to inject the medicine.
dosing: The dose depends on your condition. For most arthritis conditions, the starting dose is usually 400 mg (given as two 200 mg injections) at weeks 0, 2, and 4, followed by a maintenance dose of 200 mg every 2 weeks or 400 mg every 4 weeks. For Crohn's disease, the starting dose is 400 mg at weeks 0, 2, and 4, then 400 mg every 4 weeks if the medicine is working. Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you, so always follow your personal prescription.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then continue on your regular schedule. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your normal schedule. Do not inject two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store certolizumab pegol in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. If needed, you can store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 10 days, but do not put it back in the refrigerator after this. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used syringes and pens safely in a puncture-resistant sharps container — do not throw them in regular trash.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive live vaccines (such as shingles vaccine Zostavax, MMR, or nasal flu vaccine) while using this medicine, as it weakens your immune system. Avoid close contact with people who have active infections, including colds, flu, or chickenpox. Tell your doctor before having any surgery or dental procedures. Avoid activities that raise your risk of getting cuts or infections. Do not start this medicine if you have an active infection of any kind.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you notice: signs of serious infection such as fever, chills, persistent cough, night sweats, or unusual tiredness; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face or throat; chest pain or shortness of breath; numbness or tingling in your arms or legs; vision changes; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; or any unusual lumps or skin changes, as this medicine may slightly raise the risk of certain cancers. Also call your doctor if you develop new or worsening heart failure symptoms such as swelling in your legs or ankles.
when_it_works: Some people begin to feel improvement in symptoms within 2 to 4 weeks, but it may take up to 3 months to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better. Continue following up with your doctor regularly while using this medicine.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. If you receive certolizumab pegol during pregnancy, tell your baby's pediatrician, as it may affect the baby's immune system for several months after birth. Breastfeeding: Certolizumab pegol appears to pass very little into breast milk, but discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children. Elderly: Older adults may have a higher risk of serious infections; use with caution and follow up closely with your doctor. Tuberculosis (TB): Your doctor will test you for TB before starting this medicine. If you have a history of TB or a positive TB test, you may need treatment before starting certolizumab pegol.
